The committee has been working since 2024 to turn scattered CH₄ and N₂O processing practice into shared guidance, open tools, and, over time, updates to community datasets such as [FLUXNET-CH₄](https://fluxnet.org/data/fluxnet-ch4-community-product/).

## Three work areas

The work is organized into three structured areas, each with its own page in the [guide](guide/index.qmd):

- **[High-frequency preprocessing](guide/high-frequency.qmd)** of raw eddy-covariance data, including time-lag handling and methods that can retain more high-quality records.
- **[Half-hourly post-processing](guide/half-hourly.qmd):** quality control of 30-minute fluxes, the still-open question of u\* filtering for CH₄ and N₂O, gap-filling, and uncertainty.
- **[Ancillary variables](guide/ancillary.qmd),** launched after a full-committee discussion in September 2024, to identify which extra measurements most help people interpret and gap-fill non-CO₂ fluxes.

A longer-term goal is alignment with [ONEFlux](https://github.com/fluxnet/ONEFlux), the community processing pipeline used for FLUXNET carbon and energy products. For FLUXNET-CH₄ version 2.0, the group has committed to machine-learning approaches to gap-filling.

## Workshops

- **FLUXNET-CH₄ v2.0 Data Processing Workshop**, Berkeley, 21–23 October 2024 (hybrid; more than 100 participants).
- **FLUXNET Workshop**, Brisbane, 2025.
- **Volkswagen Foundation workshop on advancing data processing**, Hannover, 2026.

## Scientific progress

Progress so far is real but still developing. In brief:

- **High-frequency preprocessing.** Wavelet approaches can retain records that conventional stationarity or turbulence flags would otherwise discard. There has also been work on time-lag detection for closed-path laser analyzers, including high-pass filtered lag correction as implemented in tools such as [eddy4R](https://github.com/NEONScience/eddy4R).
- **Machine-learning gap-filling.** Pipelines are being integrated for community use. Results were still preliminary at the time of the 2026 summary, so no performance numbers are reported here.
- **Low and negative fluxes.** An active discussion addresses how to handle small and negative fluxes, which matter for upland sites and for the upland–wetland continuum, not only for large wetland sources.

## Open challenges

The committee has been candid about what is hard:

- Coordinating a global volunteer group across many time zones.
- Balancing new methods against the need for a standardized, comparable product.
- Developing robust uncertainty quantification for CH₄ and N₂O, which is not as settled as it is for CO₂.

## Where the work is heading

The near-term path described in 2026 is to consolidate guidance (including this public getting-started site), develop synthesis and position papers, and keep moving FLUXNET-CH₄ version 2 toward a community-wide release that new sites can join.
